finding.claim: The OAuth2 login 'state' value is also the post-login session ID. It is created before authentication, never rotated, and written to Info/Debug logs, so anyone who learns it can take over the session once the victim finishes login. This is session fixation plus a leak of a bearer credential.
finding.source: The pre-auth state/cookie value `olivetin-sid-oauth`. An attacker learns it from the IdP authorize URL, referrer or IdP logs, OliveTin Info logs, or by fixing it in the victim's browser through cookie injection. Precondition: the victim completes an OAuth2 login with that state.
finding.sink: CheckUserFromOAuth2Cookie -> lookupOAuth2UserByState returns an AuthenticatedUser with the victim's Username and Usergroup for whoever presents that cookie value, and every authenticated API action and ACL decision then runs as the victim.

trace.note: state = randString(16) is generated in HandleOAuthLogin before any authentication
registeredStates[state] is created with an empty Username and is later reused as the session
The same value is set as the cookie olivetin-sid-oauth
The state is logged at Info; line 309 logs it again together with the token code at Debug
The state is sent in the browser redirect to the IdP via AuthCodeURL(state)
The callback writes the victim's Username into the pre-existing state entry; the ID is not regenerated and the entry is not consumed
Any request carrying the cookie value is authenticated as that user

finding.guards_checked: The state==cookie comparison (190-192) only proves the callback came from the browser that holds the cookie. It is not a defence against fixation, because the attacker can hold the same value. The cookie is HttpOnly and Lax, which does not stop log or referrer leakage or cookie tossing. There is no session regeneration after login. States older than 15 minutes are swept, which bounds the window but does not remove the issue.

finding.claim: The client-controlled request header `provider` is copied into AuthenticatedUser.Provider. IsSystemExecution() and IsGuest() trust Provider == "system", so a header-authenticated user can claim to be a system user and skip the 'justification required' control.
finding.source: An HTTP request header named `provider: system`. Precondition: header authentication is enabled (AuthHttpHeaderUsername set, so Username is non-empty) and the reverse proxy does not strip a client-supplied `provider` header. Header auth always trusts the proxy for username and group, but `provider` is an extra, undocumented trusted header.
finding.sink: validateJustificationRequired -> justificationProvided returns true because executor.IsSystemExecution(user) is true. StartAction then runs an action that requires a justification with an empty justification. The Provider is also reflected into logs and WhoAmI.

trace.note: u.Provider = getHeaderKeyOrEmpty(headers, "provider"), taken from the request
The chain accepts the user when Username != ""; Provider is passed through unvalidated
IsSystemExecution returns true when Provider == "system" and Username != "guest"
justificationProvided is satisfied by IsSystemExecution, so an empty justification is accepted
StartAction enforces the justification requirement only through this check

finding.guards_checked: There is no allowlist for the provider header value. The executor's ResolveJustification also gives default text to system-named users, but only by username. Nothing else binds Provider to a trusted source.

finding.claim: GetEntities and GetEntity perform no per-user authorization on entity data. Any caller who passes checkDashboardAccess, including a guest when guests are not required to log in, receives all fields of all entity instances. When no properties are configured, serializeEntityFields returns every field. This ignores the View ACLs on the actions and dashboards that use those entities.
finding.source: An unauthenticated or low-privilege API caller sending GetEntities/GetEntity with an arbitrary entity type and key. Precondition: the default configuration with guests allowed and defaultPermissions view=true, or an ACL that denies the caller view of every action using the entity.
finding.sink: buildSortedEntityInstances / buildEntityResponse -> entityFieldsForResponse / serializeEntityFields: all entity data from the entity files (hosts, containers, and similar) is returned.

trace.note: user := UserFromApiCall; only checkDashboardAccess(user) is applied
entities.GetEntities() returns the global map with no ACL filtering
With no properties configured, all instances and their fields are returned
GetEntity looks up the entity by request type and key, again with no ACL check
serializeEntityFields dumps every field of the entity as a string

finding.guards_checked: checkDashboardAccess only blocks guests when AuthRequireGuestsToLogin is set. relatedActionsForEntity does apply userCanViewAction, but the entity fields themselves are not filtered. The acl package has no entity permission.

finding.claim: The values of all action arguments, including `password` and `very_dangerous_raw_string` types, are logged in clear text at Debug level. The code elsewhere redacts them from the command log and from stored log entries, so this bypasses the intended redaction and violates the policy of not logging sensitive data.
finding.source: A StartAction/webhook argument value of type password, supplied by any user who can run the action. Precondition: debug logging is enabled and the attacker or an operator can read the logs.
finding.sink: log.WithFields({"name": arg.Name, "value": values[arg.Name]}).Debugf("Arg assigned") in validateArguments, and the same call in parseActionArguments at line 96.

trace.note: StartAction builds args from req.Msg.Arguments
handleExecBranch -> parseActionExec
validateArguments(values, action)
The raw value is logged with no check of arg.Type == "password"
The shell branch logs the raw value in the same way

finding.guards_checked: redactShellCommand and argumentTypeStorableInLog cover the command line and the log store, but not these two log calls. The log level is Debug, so this only applies when debug logging is enabled.

finding.claim: The log-save filename is built from the action title after entity templating, with no sanitisation. If entity data contains `../` or path separators, stepSaveLog writes outside the configured results or output directory, creating files with a `.yaml` or `.log` suffix whose content comes from the command output or log entry.
finding.source: A field of an entity file used in an entity-bound action's title template (for example `{{ .CurrentEntity.name }}`). Precondition: saveLogs.resultsDirectory or outputDirectory is configured, and the entity data is influenced by an untrusted party (for example names generated from container, host or user-supplied data).
finding.sink: os.WriteFile(path.Join(dir, filename+".yaml"|".log"), ...) in saveLogResults and saveLogOutput.

trace.note: entry.ActionTitle = ParseTemplateOfActionBeforeExec(Action.Title, Binding.Entity), which includes entity data
filename = ActionTitle.StartedUnix.TrackingID, with no sanitisation
path.Join(dir, filename+".yaml") normalises `..` and so escapes dir
path.Join(dir, filename+".log") has the same escape

finding.guards_checked: No basename or separator stripping and no prefix check against dir. The tracking-ID part is validated, but the title part is not. The trigger requires the entity data to be attacker-influenced and saveLogs to be enabled.

finding.claim: The webhook `matchHeaders` and `matchQuery` values of every action are returned in the action protobuf to every viewer. If an operator uses these as a shared secret (for example matchHeaders: X-Token: <secret>, or matchQuery token=<secret>, with authType none), the secret is disclosed to anyone who can load the dashboard or GetActionBinding, including guests. They can then trigger the webhook.
finding.source: Any caller of GetDashboard, GetActionBinding or GetEntity (related actions) who can view the action. Precondition: a webhook config uses matchHeaders or matchQuery as a de facto credential.
finding.sink: pb.ExecOnWebhooks[].MatchHeaders / MatchQuery in the API response. The attacker then POSTs to /webhooks with the learned header or query value, which passes the unauthenticated matcher and runs the action as system user 'webhook'.

trace.note: buildAction always calls applyActionExecTriggers(&btn, action)
Copies wh.MatchHeaders and wh.MatchQuery verbatim into the response
Matching headers are a plain comparison and do not authenticate
With AuthType empty or none, Verify returns true
The action then runs as auth.UserFromSystem("webhook")

finding.guards_checked: Only the View ACL gates the response, and the default is view=true. Whether this is exploitable depends on the operator treating match values as secrets. Properly configured HMAC, bearer or basic auth is unaffected.
